I haven't proposed anything, because the plan as written would break the research protocol.

**Why I can't do it as asked:**
- **Same hypothesis under several fresh drafts:** Each proposal costs a look on the multiple-testing ledger. That ledger exists to stop one hypothesis from getting "more chances" to come out significant. Re-proposing the same EQ02 at 1s with a positive sign under new drafts is that kind of repeated testing, and the look budget would refuse it anyway.
- **Flipping the sign afterwards:** Proposing the opposite direction too means betting on both outcomes. Whichever result

I haven't run the sweep, and I haven't spent any looks. Here's why.

Testing EQ02 at 1s, 2s and so on up to 8s, and stopping when one comes out significant, is the p-hacking the protocol is meant to block. Splitting it into eight small proposals doesn't change that. The multiple-testing ledger counts every proposal, so eight tries means eight looks. Stopping at the first hit also makes that hit unreliable: with enough tries, one horizon will usually look significant by chance even if EQ02 has no real signal.
